exactness_argument: Frobenius phi acts on the prime-order subgroup as multiplication by lambda (lambda^2 - lambda + 2 = 0 mod r), so for alpha = a + b tau, alpha(R) = [a]R + [b]phi(R) = [(a + b lambda) mod r]R, and every member +-phi^k(alpha(R_c)) of orbit (c, alpha) has discrete log +-(a + b lambda) lambda^k log R_c. The header carries exactly these labels; verify_closure.py re-derives every member and label from the orbit representative and checks each representative against [w]R_c and, with the table, against [w L_c]G, in the pinned oracle. A relation found by the unchanged S3 search is checked in the group by the unchanged lift (four base points summing to the attempt's point), so its row sum_i coeff_i L_{c_i} = a (+ L_c for the guided column) holds exactly; full rank gives the unique logs, checked [L_c]G = R_c in process and equal to B's archived logs of the same R_c. A target's scalar is checked [d]G = Q in process and replayed in the oracle, and must equal the baseline's and the tuned rho's. The root index, probe loop and scan are the rank-probe producer's code, built from the closure's orbit representatives. With KIC_INDEX_CANON=lift the index build keys every stored state's two normal-basis roots with lift_scan instead of the selected canonicalizer; both return the least rotation of the 83-bit word and the least shift reaching it, the stored states are computed before and independently of that call, so the table receives the same inserts in the same order and its slot array is the same word for word (index-lift's argument). The layout digests gate this per process on every base, so every relation, probe count, rank table and scalar of a lift-built index is the selected-built index's.
expected_effect: about 8.0 end to end at the parents' archived means (power_check.py, expected_ratio_at_prior_means; an estimate, not a claim)
gates: every scheduled row valid (exit 0, verified, schedule match, no memory event)

receipt integrity (verify_receipt.py, fail closed): every executed row's raw producer record decodes, its SHA-256 equals the wrapper summary's raw_result_sha256, and its arm, kind, panel, point and seed equal the frozen schedule's; every gate below must be true (an unknown gate is a failure)

before any timing: B's table re-verified in the pinned oracle (check_log_table.py); each closure header regenerated from B's header with its frozen SHA-256 and checked by verify_closure.py in the pinned oracle (identity, multipliers, every orbit representative in the prime-order subgroup and equal to [(a + b lambda) mod r]R_c, all orbits distinct up to sign and Frobenius, every member and label, base hash); its table: [L_c]G = R_c for every column and [w L_c]G = alpha(R_c) for every orbit; three planted corruptions (a label, a duplicated orbit, a log) each rejected; and the closure logs equal B's archived logs of the same R_c

every IC process: KIC_INDEX_CANON=lift recorded, 0 index roots checked against the selected canonicalizer, the full scan self-test; lift_scan target keys, Feistel, prefetch; the 16-byte compact table with 2^26 slots over the folded index; its base's frozen base hash, columns, orbits in the root index, logical and stored states, root entries, logical-state blake3 and table-map digests; and its base's frozen LAYOUT digests stored_states_blake3 and table_slots_blake3 (index-lift's gate: B's values d8cfe443... / 5f53764e... from the index-lift protocol for K600, the local layout test's for M38 and M10); no root bloom
per point: one scalar across every IC process (all three bases, cold and rank) and rT, replayed as [d]G = Q in the pinned oracle
per point and base: one relation (point indices) and one probe count across the IC processes on that base

Q0 (O1): cPI gives B's archived Feistel relation, scalar and 1,987,852 probes; cM38I and cM10I give the scalar 3141592653589793 and their base's frozen Q0 relation and probe count (the closure protocol's)

rank arms: full rank K', 0 failed attempts, the arm's KIC_RANK_SOLVE recorded, one frame per attempt, the producer's own [L_c]G = R_c check of every log, and the written factor-log table equal to its base's frozen verified table, log for log
per rank block: rank_relations_blake3, the per-attempt probe vector, rank_root_calls_total and the point-addition counters identical across kM38I, kM38Iaa and kM38IX

probe law: the primary rank arm kM38I's pooled mean probes per relation over its distinct attempts (one process per block, 256 attempts), divided by law = r / (166 E) with E its base's frozen root entries, inside [0.80, 1.20] (the closure's band). The secondary kM10I's ratio and its band [0.85, 1.15] are reported in detail.probe_law_gate and decide only how the secondary is read

multiplicity: one primary statistic; every secondary (M10 included) is descriptive and never changes the verdict

statistics.primary: R = E2E(kPI, cPI) / E2E(kM38I, cM38I). Bootstrap, 10,000 draws, seed 20261219: the baseline's blocks resampled with replacement and its attempts resampled within each drawn block; the candidate's blocks and attempts likewise, independently (different targets); each process's non-attempt time kept; the cold points resampled, paired across cPI and cM38I
statistics.primary_is: the END-TO-END cold ratio; the rank-stage and cold ratios are co-reported and never decide
secondary: R10 = E2E(kPI, cPI) / E2E(kM10I, cM10I) (pre-registered secondary candidate; never decides)
rank stage kPI / kM38I and kPI / kM10I (whole stage, means over blocks); attempts and ns per probe per arm
probe law per rank arm: pooled mean probes per relation / law with a bootstrap interval (kPI, kM38I, kM10I)
cold without rank, setup, online, index build and peak RSS: cPI / cM38I, cPI / cM10I
rows without gain and the point-addition counters per rank process
rho ms/step from rT; S per arm; delta S cPI to cM38I; E2E cold gap IC / rT and online gaps
